heading: Two pointers with a gap
body:
To remove the nth node from the end **in one pass**, create a gap of n nodes between two pointers.

- Move `fast` n steps ahead first
- Move both together until `fast` hits the end
- `slow` lands right before the target node

Use a **dummy node** so removing the head works the same as any other node.

heading: Why the dummy node trick works
body:
Without a dummy, removing the head is a special case (no predecessor).

With `dummy.next = head`, every node—even the head—has a predecessor. Your removal logic `slow.next = slow.next.next` works uniformly.

Return `dummy.next` to get the new head.

label: Crux · Python
code:
dummy = ListNode(0)
dummy.next = head
fast = slow = dummy

# Create n-node gap
for _ in range(n):
    fast = fast.next

# Move together until fast at end
while fast.next:
    fast = fast.next
    slow = slow.next

# Remove target
slow.next = slow.next.next
return dummy.next

q: Why do we use a dummy node in this approach?
options: To eliminate special case handling when removing the head node
To improve the time complexity from O(n²) to O(n)
To reduce the space complexity to O(1)
explain: The dummy node acts as a predecessor to the head, allowing us to treat all nodes uniformly—even when removing the head.
